stages.name: In revolt
stages.desc: Independent of Persia or risen against it

stages.name: Persian
stages.desc: Ruled by the Achaemenid Great King and his satraps

stages.name: Macedonian
stages.desc: Conquered by Alexander and ruled by his governors

stages.name: City-kings
stages.desc: Phoenician or Cypriot city-kings on their own thrones, under an overlord

stages.name: Ptolemaic
stages.desc: Held by Ptolemy, Macedonian ruler of Egypt

stages.name: Antigonid
stages.desc: Held by Antigonus the One-Eyed and his son Demetrius

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: The nine city-kings of Cyprus rise against Persia
Idrieus of Caria and Greek mercenaries force the Cypriot kings back under Persia
The Cypriot kings join Alexander with their fleets at Tyre and keep their thrones
Ptolemy kills or deposes the kings of Kition, Lapithos and Marion
Demetrius destroys Ptolemy's fleet off Salamis and takes Cyprus

states.name: Israel
timeline: The coastal cities (Akko, Dor, Joppa) are ruled from Persia's Syrian satrapy
Alexander besieges Gaza and the coast submits
Ptolemy takes Coele-Syria
Antigonus conquers the coast
Ptolemy defeats Demetrius at Gaza and occupies the coast
Ptolemy razes Akko and Joppa as he retreats; Antigonus returns

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Gaza and the Persian province of Judah (Yehud)
Gaza falls after a two-month siege
Ptolemy takes Coele-Syria; Jerusalem falls to him on a Sabbath
Antigonus conquers Coele-Syria
Battle of Gaza: Ptolemy and Seleucus defeat Demetrius
Ptolemy pulls back to Egypt, slighting Gaza and Samaria

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Sidon, under King Tennes, leads the Phoenician cities in revolt against Persia
Betrayed by Tennes, Sidon burns; Persia installs Evagoras, then Straton II as king
Straton is deposed; Hephaestion makes the gardener Abdalonymus king of Sidon under Alexander
Ptolemy's general Nicanor seizes Phoenicia; Abdalonymus keeps his throne
Antigonus takes the coast and builds a war fleet from Lebanese cedar
After his victory at Gaza, Ptolemy occupies Sidon and Tyre; Abdalonymus dies about now
Ptolemy withdraws; Antigonus holds Phoenicia again

states.name: Syria
timeline: Damascus and the Syrian interior stay loyal to the Persian satrap
Arados and the northern Phoenician cities submit to Artaxerxes III
After Issus, Parmenion seizes Persian treasure at Damascus
Ptolemy captures the satrap Laomedon and takes Syria
Antigonus drives Ptolemy's garrisons out of Syria
Antigonus founds his new capital, Antigonia, on the Orontes

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Anatolia is ruled by Persian satraps and the Carian dynasts
Granicus, Halicarnassus and Issus put Asia Minor in Alexander's hands
After Antipater's death, Antigonus makes himself master of Asia Minor

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Ammon and the desert fringes of Persia's Syrian satrapy; Nabataean Arabs in the south
The lands east of the Jordan pass, loosely, to Alexander
Loosely held by Ptolemy's Coele-Syria
Loosely held by Antigonus
Antigonus' raids on the Nabataeans of Petra fail

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Pharaoh Nectanebo II rules an independent Egypt and repels a Persian invasion
Artaxerxes III reconquers Egypt; Nectanebo, the last native pharaoh, flees south
Egypt opens its gates to Alexander
Ptolemy becomes satrap of Egypt
Antigonus' invasion of Egypt stalls at the Nile

events.title: Sidon revolts
events.text: King Tennes of Sidon burns the Persian royal park and expels the Persian officials.

events.title: Egypt repels Persia
events.text: Nectanebo II throws back a Persian attempt to reconquer Egypt.

events.title: Cyprus rises
events.text: The nine city-kings of Cyprus join the revolt against the Great King.

events.title: Sidon burns
events.text: Betrayed by Tennes, the Sidonians set fire to their city; Diodorus counts forty thousand dead.

events.title: Tennes executed
events.text: Artaxerxes III has the traitor king put to death once the city is taken.

events.title: Cyprus subdued
events.text: Idrieus of Caria and the Athenian Phocion besiege Salamis and end the Cypriot revolt.

events.title: Egypt reconquered
events.text: Artaxerxes III takes Pelusium and Memphis; Nectanebo II flees to Nubia.

events.title: Siege of Perinthus
events.text: Persian satraps send men and money to help Perinthus resist Philip II of Macedon.

events.title: The Granicus
events.text: Alexander crosses into Asia and defeats the Persian satraps on the Granicus river.

events.title: Halicarnassus
events.text: Alexander besieges and burns the Carian capital.

events.title: Gordian knot
events.text: At Gordium Alexander cuts, or unties, the famous knot.

events.title: Battle of Issus
events.text: Alexander defeats Darius III; the Great King flees, leaving his family behind.

events.title: Damascus taken
events.text: Parmenion seizes Darius' baggage train and treasure at Damascus.

events.title: Byblos and Arados
events.text: The kings of Byblos and Arados surrender their cities to Alexander.

events.title: Sidon opens its gates
events.text: Sidon welcomes Alexander; its pro-Persian king Straton is deposed.

events.title: The gardener king
events.text: Hephaestion offers the throne to Abdalonymus, found drawing water in his garden.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: Alexander builds a mole to the island city; after seven months Tyre falls.

events.title: Siege of Gaza
events.text: Gaza holds out for two months before it is stormed.

events.title: Alexandria founded
events.text: Alexander lays out a new city on the Egyptian coast.

events.title: Alexander leaves
events.text: Alexander crosses the Euphrates at Thapsacus on his way to his last battle with Darius.

events.title: Sidon's mint
events.text: Sidon strikes silver coins in Alexander's name, dated by the years of Abdalonymus' reign.

events.title: Ships for Babylon
events.text: Phoenician shipwrights build a fleet that is carried overland to the Euphrates for Alexander.

events.title: Alexander dies
events.text: Alexander dies in Babylon; Ptolemy takes Egypt as satrap.

events.title: Alexander's body
events.text: Ptolemy hijacks Alexander's funeral cart in Syria and buries him at Memphis.

events.title: Ptolemy takes Syria
events.text: Ptolemy's general Nicanor captures the satrap Laomedon and occupies Phoenicia.

events.title: Jerusalem taken
events.text: Ptolemy captures Jerusalem, by tradition on the Sabbath.

events.title: Antigonus marches
events.text: Antigonus the One-Eyed sweeps down the coast and drives out Ptolemy's garrisons.

events.title: Cedar fleet
events.text: Antigonus orders warships built from Lebanese cedar at Tripolis, Byblos and Sidon.

events.title: Tyre besieged again
events.text: Antigonus takes Tyre after a fifteen-month siege.

events.title: Cyprus purged
events.text: Ptolemy kills Pumiathon of Kition and abolishes several Cypriot kingdoms.

events.title: Battle of Gaza
events.text: Ptolemy and Seleucus defeat Demetrius, son of Antigonus.

events.title: Sidon taken
events.text: Ptolemy's army occupies Sidon and Tyre; Abdalonymus' reign ends about this time.

events.title: Raid on Petra
events.text: Antigonus sends troops against the Nabataeans of Petra; they are beaten back.

events.title: Ptolemy retreats
events.text: Ptolemy razes Akko, Joppa, Samaria and Gaza and falls back to Egypt.

events.title: Peace of the dynasts
events.text: The Successors make a short-lived peace; Antigonus keeps Syria and Phoenicia.

events.title: Nicocles of Paphos
events.text: Ptolemy forces the king of Paphos to take his own life.

events.title: Ptolemy in Cilicia
events.text: Ptolemy's fleet raids the coasts of Cilicia and takes Phaselis.

events.title: Antigonia founded
events.text: Antigonus founds a royal capital on the Orontes.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.text: Demetrius destroys Ptolemy's fleet off Cyprus.

events.title: Kings at last
events.text: After Salamis, Antigonus and Demetrius take the title of king; the Successors follow.

events.title: Egypt holds
events.text: Antigonus' invasion of Egypt founders at the Nile, near Pelusium.

chartNote: Share of the area of eight present-day countries (Lebanon, Syria, Turkey, Cyprus, Israel, Palestine, Jordan and Egypt), by the power that held most of each. Regions are today's boundaries, not ancient ones; control was often partial, contested or nominal (above all in the deserts of Syria and Jordan), and dates mark turning points. A simplification: large Turkey and Egypt dominate the shares.
